sources.title: Perspective: OLED Displays Singing with the Blues
sources.abstract: While blue pixels consume approximately 50% of the energy of organic light-emitting diode (OLED) display front planes, in the 25 years since their invention, 100% internal efficiency phosphorescent OLEDs (PHOLEDs) have not met the stability standards necessary for their adoption. In this perspective, we discuss the significant progress and challenges encountered during this long journey of exploration and discovery. Today, using a combination of solutions including robust molecular design, graded doping of the emission layer, increasing the optical density of states to decrease the triplet radiative lifetime, and employing light outcoupling schemes, deep blue PHOLEDs are now achieving lifetimes approaching those of their green analogs. This perspective elaborates on the challenges and opportunities confronting further development of triplet-controlled emitters, including PHOLEDs using heavy-metal phosphors and thermally activated delayed fluorescent OLEDs. We also address some persistent problems commonly found in the literature concerning the measurement of quantum efficiency and operational lifetime.

sources.title: Physics-Constrained Graph Neural Networks for Spatio-Temporal Prediction of Drop Impact on OLED Display Panels
sources.abstract: This study aims to predict the spatio-temporal evolution of physical quantities observed in multi-layered display panels subjected to the drop impact of a ball. To model these complex interactions, graph neural networks have emerged as promising tools, effectively representing objects and their relationships as graph structures. In particular, MeshGraphNets (MGNs) excel in capturing dynamics in dynamic physics simulations using irregular mesh data. However, conventional MGNs often suffer from non-physical artifacts, such as the penetration of overlapping objects. To resolve this, we propose a physics-constrained MGN that mitigates these penetration issues while maintaining high level of accuracy in temporal predictions. Furthermore, to enhance the model's robustness, we explore noise injection strategies with varying magnitudes and different combinations of targeted components, such as the ball, the plate, or both. In addition, our analysis on model stability in spatio-temporal predictions reveals that during the inference, deriving next time-step node positions by predicting relative changes (e.g., displacement or velocity) between the current and future states yields superior accuracy compared to direct absolute position predictions. This approach consistently shows greater stability and reliability in determining subsequent node positions across various scenarios. Building on this validated model, we evaluate its generalization performance by examining its ability to extrapolate with respect to design variables. Furthermore, the physics-constrained MGN serves as a near real-time emulator for the design optimization of multi-layered OLED display panels, where thickness variables are optimized to minimize stress in the light-emitting materials. It outperforms conventional MGN in optimization tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness for practical design applications.

sources.title: The Steady Evolution of OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Abstract OLED's flexibility has made it the dominant display technology in premium smartphones. As the technology continues to improve, it is gaining traction in the automotive, IT, and AR/VR markets.

sources.title: ReHome Earth: A VR-Based Concept Validation for AI-Driven Space Homesickness Interventions
sources.abstract: Space exploration has advanced rapidly, but the emotional needs of astronauts on long-duration missions remain underexplored. We present ReHome Earth, a dual-component design approach addressing space homesickness: 1) a future-oriented installation concept integrating transparent OLED displays with spaceship windows for real-time Earth connectivity, and 2) a functional VR prototype simulating astronaut isolation for testing AI-generated content effectiveness. Since accessing astronauts during missions is impossible, we conducted concept validation with terrestrial participants experiencing geographic displacement. Through evaluation with 84 proxy participants and 6 HCI experts, we demonstrate strong emotional resonance and validate three design implications: emotional pacing mechanisms, explainable biophysical feedback systems, and evolution from individual tools to collective affective infrastructure. Our contributions include a technically feasible space installation concept, a functional VR prototype for space HCI research, and empirical insights into the design of AI-driven emotional support systems for extreme isolation environments.

sources.title: Color Calibration Methods For OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Accurate color reproduction on a display requires an inverse display model, mapping colorimetric values (e.g. CIE XYZ) into RGB values driving the display. To create such a model, we collected a large dataset of display color measurements for a high refresh-rate 4-primary OLED display. We demonstrated that, unlike traditional LCD displays, multi-primary OLED display color responses are non-additive and non-linear for some colors. We tested the performances of different regression methods: polynomial regression, look-up tables, multi-layer perceptrons, and others. The best-performing models were additionally validated on newly measured (unseen) test colors. We found that the performances of several variations of 4th-degree polynomial models were comparable to the look-up table and machine-learning-based models while being less resource-intensive.

sources.title: Treat-through OLED Displays: Dosimetry and performance of OLED AVATAR screens for Megavoltage Radiotherapy
sources.abstract: The AVATAR system utilizes a radiolucent video display to help relax and immobilize pediatric patients during radiotherapy. This study investigates the use of OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) displays, which offer superior image quality and faster alignment compared to traditional projector-based systems, albeit with slightly increased thickness. The dose perturbations caused by these screens were assessed to evaluate their suitability for radiotherapy. A 20 cm OLED screen was positioned in the patient's line of sight, between the patient's head and the radiation source. The screen comprises a 0.25 mm thick flexible OLED panel and a custom carbon fiber backing (0.3 to 0.6 mm thick), with most electronic components relocated via ribbon cable. 6 MV portal images were captured with and without the screen to create transmission maps. Additionally, parallel plate ion chamber measurements were taken at the surface and at depth in a solid water phantom. The OLED's radiation tolerance was tested with a 100 Gy dose delivery and 12 months of use in an active radiotherapy linac vault. The portal image transmission maps indicated an average attenuation difference of 0.3\% (SD = 0.37 \%) between measurements with and without the AVATAR screen, with a maximum point attenuation of 3\%. Ion chamber measurements revealed a 0.31\% decrease in dose at 2 cm depth and a 7.04 \% increase at the surface under an anterior-posterior beam. For a VMAT arc, the dose difference was 0.04 \% at 2 cm depth and 0.1\% at the phantom surface. The minimal dose deviations indicate that these screens are suitable for megavoltage arc therapy without significantly affecting the target dose. While surface dose is slightly increased for static anterior beams, it remains low. For lower photon energies or particle beams, larger perturbations may occur, necessitating further measurements or beam entry avoidance.

sources.title: MAX OLED Solution for Next‐Generation OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Abstract A breakthrough in OLED display pixel architecture and manufacturing technology will enhance display performance and enable a wider range of applications.

sources.title: CosmicWatch: The Desktop Muon Detector(v3X)
sources.abstract: The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector (v3X) is a compact, low-cost, and portable device designed for detecting ionizing radiation, including cosmic-ray muons. Building on previous iterations, the v3X introduces significant hardware and firmware improvements that enhance sensitivity, usability, and data acquisition capabilities. The detector integrates a plastic scintillator and silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), custom designed electronics for signal processing, onboard data storage, OLED display, environmental sensors, and USB connectivity. With a total component cost under \$100 and a build time suitable for high school students, the v3X is ideal for education, outreach, and introductory research applications in particle and astroparticle physics. This paper details the design, performance, and potential use cases of the v3X, supported by example measurements demonstrating its functionality.

sources.title: The application of organic materials used in OLED display
sources.abstract: Based on the advantages of higher luminous efficiency, lower energy consumption and ecological protection, the organic light-emitting diode (OLED) has become a new type of display in mobile OLED device, which was also called as the dream display. Many organic materials including polyimide (PI), photoresist (PR), photosensitive polyimide (PSPI), OLED emissive layer materials, inkjet printing (IJP), optical clear adhesive (OCA) and undercut pixel definition layer (undercut PDL) have been introduced during the manufacturing process of OLED display. The pol less progress (PLP) technology had also been introduced in the OLED display by replacing the polarizer, which also introduced a few new organic materials such as black pixel definition layer (BPDL), black matrix (BM) and color film (CF) and applied in the OLED display. In this paper, the author had a review on the organic materials used in the manufacturing process of an OLED display, which included the application of organic materials used in the array structure, the emissive layer (EL) structure, the display of things (DOT) structure and the new OLED display based on the PLP technology. The application of organic material undercut PDL which was used for forming the protruding spacing columns between pixels to prevent the lateral leakage of current between adjacent pixels was also described detailed in this paper.

sources.title: Modeling and Exploiting the Time Course of Chromatic Adaptation for Display Power Optimizations in Virtual Reality
sources.abstract: We introduce a gaze-tracking--free method to reduce OLED display power consumption in VR with minimal perceptual impact. This technique exploits the time course of chromatic adaptation, the human visual system's ability to maintain stable color perception under changing illumination. To that end, we propose a novel psychophysical paradigm that models how human adaptation state changes with the scene illuminant. We exploit this model to compute an optimal illuminant shift trajectory, controlling the rate and extent of illumination change, to reduce display power under a given perceptual loss budget. Our technique significantly improves the perceptual quality over prior work that applies illumination shifts instantaneously. Our technique can also be combined with prior work on luminance dimming to reduce display power by 31% with no statistical loss of perceptual quality.

sources.title: The Design of a Detection Robot with OLED Display
sources.abstract: OLED display has the advantages of self-illumination, wide viewing angle, fast response, small size, small weight, flexibility. It is a huge breakthrough in the field of display technology, and enhances the visual enjoyment and on-the-spot experience of people. With the rapid development of science and technology, the combination of OLED and robot has attracted attention from most of the fields. In this paper, the working principle, advantages and main application fields of OLED devices are introduced, and a detection robot with OLED is designed. The detection robot can accurately control the speed of the motor and the angle of the steering gear within a distance of 1,000 meters, and receive the images from airborne cameras in real time.

sources.title: IoT-Enabled Smart Car Parking System through Integrated Sensors and Mobile Applications
sources.abstract: Due to more population congestion and car ownership, the provision of parking spaces for vehicles is becoming a crucial factor. This paper aims to present a novel Internet of Things (IoT)--based smart car parking system that can effectively manage these problems with the help of sensor technology and automation. Infrared (IR) sensors, DHT22 sensors, MQ-2 gas sensors, and servo motors are used in the parking space. An OLED display shows the status of parking slots in real-time. Communicating with a mobile application through the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol enables the efficient exchange of data. As a result, this innovative solution optimizes parking space, increases efficiency, and makes the parking lot more comfortable. This IoT system allows real-time monitoring and automation of parked cars as well as fast response to dynamic changes in environmental conditions, setting a new standard for smart parking systems.

sources.title: Polaritons Enable Brilliant Colors in OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Abstract Microcavities can be used to narrow the broad emission spectra of OLED displays—but at the cost of angular dependence. Polaritons solve this issue and enable angle‐independent and highly efficient OLED emissions.

sources.title: STM32-Based Smart Waste Bin for Hygienic Disposal Using Embedded Sensing and Automated Control
sources.abstract: The increasing demand for hygienic and contactless solutions in public and private environments has encouraged the development of automated systems for everyday applications. This paper presents the design and implementation of a motion- sensing automatic waste bin using an STM32 microcontroller, ultrasonic sensors, and a servo motor. The system detects user presence through ultrasonic sensing and automatically opens the bin lid using a servo motor controlled by the microcontroller. An additional ultrasonic sensor is used to monitor the internal waste level of the bin, while an OLED display provides real- time feedback regarding system status. The proposed system offers a low-cost, reliable, and easily deployable solution for touch-free waste disposal. Experimental evaluation demonstrates fast response time, stable sensing performance, and smooth mechanical operation. The system can be effectively deployed in homes, educational institutions, hospitals, and public facilities to improve hygiene and user convenience.

sources.title: Materials to Enable Future OLED Display Evolution

sources.title: Intrinsic Limitations of Single Layer Polychromatic Metalens for Virtual Reality Visors
sources.abstract: Virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR) visors require compact and lightweight optics. Metalenses have been widely proposed as ultrathin replacements for bulky refractive eyepieces, with performance typically assessed using point spread function (PSF) and modulation transfer function (MTF) measurements. Here, we design, fabricate, and characterize a single-layer silicon nitride metalens optimized for the three emission peaks of an RGB OLED display, and benchmark it against refractive and Fresnel eyepieces. Under coherent illumination, the metalens exhibits a tightly confined PSF and strong mid-to-high spatial-frequency MTF, suggesting excellent optical performance. However, when evaluated in a realistic system-level VR testbed incorporating incoherent OLED illumination, a dynamic-pupil eye model, and near-eye-relevant focal lengths, the same device exhibits pronounced ghosting and background haze. We show that these artifacts arise from the intrinsic multifocal nature of polychromatic diffractive focusing and demonstrate that common mitigation strategies such as narrowband filtering and long-focal-length relay optics merely mask, rather than resolve, the issue. Our results establish that meta-optics for AR/VR must be evaluated under realistic system-level conditions to reveal their true imaging performance.

sources.title: OLED lifetime simulation for VR displays
sources.abstract: This paper introduces a new methodology for simulating the burn-in of an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) microdisplay used in a virtual reality (VR) headset. The proposed simulation employs the stretched exponential decay (SED) model, which is widely used to predict the degradation of the OLED device over time. Furthermore, the model integrates the impact of user head motion on VR display image content. The study defines productivity and gaming mode surrogate image content from which to simulate burn-in and applies image processing correlating to head motion data collected from a user study. The results of this study indicate that head motion has a significant impact on OLED burn-in. Given a conservative assumption for image content and head motion, the time for visual failure due to burn-in artifacts is 4 times slower than a case with stationary image content.

sources.title: Electrically driven organic laser using integrated OLED pumping
sources.abstract: Abstract Organic semiconductors are carbon-based materials that combine optoelectronic properties with simple fabrication and the scope for tuning by changing their chemical structure1–3. They have been successfully used to make organic light-emitting diodes2,4,5 (OLEDs, now widely found in mobile phone displays and televisions), solar cells1, transistors6 and sensors7. However, making electrically driven organic semiconductor lasers is very challenging8,9. It is difficult because organic semiconductors typically support only low current densities, suffer substantial absorption from injected charges and triplets, and have additional losses due to contacts10,11. In short, injecting charges into the gain medium leads to intolerable losses. Here we take an alternative approach in which charge injection and lasing are spatially separated, thereby greatly reducing losses. We achieve this by developing an integrated device structure that efficiently couples an OLED, with exceptionally high internal-light generation, with a polymer distributed feedback laser. Under the electrical driving of the integrated structure, we observe a threshold in light output versus drive current, with a narrow emission spectrum and the formation of a beam above the threshold. These observations confirm lasing. Our results provide an organic electronic device that has not been previously demonstrated, and show that indirect electrical pumping by an OLED is a very effective way of realizing an electrically driven organic semiconductor laser. This provides an approach to visible lasers that could see applications in spectroscopy, metrology and sensing.

sources.title: P‐14.14: IJP OLEDs Advanced Adaptive De‐burn‐in algorithm
sources.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers
sources.abstract: We propose a solution to IS (Image Sticking), one of the important issue in IJPOLEDs , which has various advantages over conventional vacuum deposition methods. One solution to IS is De‐burn‐in technology (DBI), but it cannot be completely improved due to deviation in OLED life characteristics. In addition, managing variations in the life characteristics mentioned above is required to ensure that DBI performance is sufficient. To solve this problem, we propose a method of DBI design based on variability. By performing a short life evaluation and measuring the initial optical characteristics of each panel during the manufacturing stage, DBI settings were implemented individually. This allows for a wide range of characteristic to be resolved. In fact, we constructed a manufacturing method, and through the introduction of the architecture, the difference in brightness due to deterioration was reduced to less than 1/3.

sources.title: Bimolecular Annihilation Processes in OLEDs
sources.abstract: This thesis investigates the physical limitations and efficiency roll-off of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) at high brightness levels. Due to the low dielectric constant of organic semiconductors, tightly bound excitons are formed, which at high current densities trigger bimolecular loss mechanisms such as triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA) and triplet–polaron annihilation (TPA). These phenomena reduce device efficiency and generate heat as well as high-energy excited states, which cause chemical damage to the materials and shorten the operational lifespan of the device. The study demonstrates that these losses can be managed by restricting exciton diffusion through host–guest systems or by accelerating radiative recombination using optical microcavities. The development of OLED devices requires a constant balance between high efficiency, durability, and manufacturing complexity. Future research should focus particularly on improving the stability of blue emitters and developing more precise kinetic models to ensure the reliability of mass-produced devices.

sources.title: Recent research on the status and advances of OLED
sources.abstract: Organic Light-Emitting Diodes (OLEDs) have already been a prominent display technology in various applications for many decades, ranging from smartphones and televisions to wearable devices and lighting. It is important to understand the current state of OLED research in order to assess its progress, identify challenges, and explore more potential ways for further development. In this paper, the significance and widespread adoption of OLED technology are briefly introduced, and its advantages over traditional display technologies are highlighted. The paper then provides a concise overview of the major components and working principles of OLEDs without delving into basic notions. The paper discusses both small molecule OLEDs (SMOLEDs) and polymer OLEDs (POLEDs), emphasizing their unique structure, characteristics and properties. Different strategies employed to enhance OLED performance is investigated, including the regulation of band gaps that influence the efficiency and brightness. This paper also focuses on the evaluation of device reliability and stability aspects. The techniques and materials employed in studies related to OLED development are also discussed with many searched experimental data and ongoing research activities. Furthermore, the research content covered the aspects of recent commercial advancements in OLED technology, such as Active matrix OLEDs (AMOLED) and Passive matrix (PMOLED). The review provides a guideline for researchers, industry professionals, and enthusiasts to better understand the OLED technology into its details, potential, and the areas that require further exploration.

sources.title: 46.1: Invited Paper: LCD Innovations vs. OLED Performance for Automotive Applications
sources.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers
sources.abstract: LCDs are today's workhorse for automotive displays. In recent years, some premium OEMs started to ship cars with OLED displays. The advantages of OLEDs compared to LCDs are short response time at low temperature (relevant for e‐mirrors) and perfect black at night as well as highly curved and transparent versions. Replacing edge‐lit backlight of LCDs by FALD (full array local dimming) results in highest luminance at acceptable halo. Furthermore, LCDs have a large supply chain, which results in competitive cost. Well‐known challenges of OLEDs deal with high luminance and temperature sensitivity, which can result in reduced lifetime (LT) incl. Burn‐In. Challenges and solutions for LCDs and OLEDs such as halo measurements and viewing angle performance will be discussed more in detail. Latest automotive demonstrators show the potential of micro‐LEDs and electrically pumped Quantum Dots (QD) displays. Both have the potential to outperform LCDs and OLEDs.

sources.title: Hyperphosphorescent OLEDs: Harnessing the Power of MR‐TADF Terminal Emitters
sources.abstract: Abstract Hyperphosphorescent organic light‐emitting diodes (HP‐OLEDs) represent an attractive solution to persistent efficiency roll‐off and device stability issues, combining phosphorescent sensitizers with fluorescent terminal emitters to achieve efficient, narrowband emission. This review discusses advances in HP‐OLEDs where the terminal emitter is a multiresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence compound. Recent breakthroughs in device performance, including examples demonstrating both high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max ) and excellent color purity, are highlighted. This review summarizes design strategies, challenges, and future directions for improving the efficiency, stability, and spectral performance of HP‐OLEDs.

sources.title: Research Progress on the Preparation of OLED Based on the Inkjet Printing
sources.abstract: Abstract Over the past few decades, organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) have demonstrated compelling technological advantages due to their ability to directly convert electrons into photons without requiring backlighting, thereby offering self‐emissive surfaces, ultrathin device profiles, compatibility with flexible substrates, high luminance, and exceptional contrast ratios (achieving true black). Today, OLEDs dominate the market for small‐scale displays such as smartphones and laptops. Propelled by the burgeoning ubiquity of the Internet of Things, OLEDs are poised to experience an exponential upsurge in prospective exigency. However, conventional thermal evaporation techniques face challenges in achieving uniform large‐area OLED fabrication, rendering mass production costly and complex—a persistent drawback hindering OLEDs from becoming the undisputed market leader. Amidst this milieu, inkjet printing (IJP) has magnetized considerable scholarly and commercial traction across the panoply of fabrication modalities, crystallizing as the pre‐eminent candidate for scalable, large‐area OLED manufacturing. This technique boasts non‐contact processing, high material utilization, and compatibility with roll‐to‐roll manufacturing. In this review, the critical parameters governing ink formulation are delineated and provide an overview of prevailing OLED device architectures. Subsequently, recent advancements are consolidate in inkjet‐printed OLED layers, culminating in a circumspect prognosis of the extant impediments and the prospective trajectory toward wholly inkjet‐patterned OLED architectures.

sources.title: The Effect of Molecular Structure on the Properties of Fluorene Derivatives for OLED Applications
sources.abstract: A new family of symmetrical fluorene derivatives with different types of substituents attached to the C-2 and C-7 positions of the fluorene core synthesized by the Sonogashira coupling reactions is reported. The electronic structures and the properties of the compounds investigated by means of photoelectron emission spectroscopy, UV-Vis absorption and photoluminescent spectroscopy as well as by DFT and TD-DFT theoretical calculations are discussed. It is shown that the nature of substituents influences the π-conjugation of the molecules. No intermolecular charge transfer within the investigated wavelength range is observed. The applicability of the synthesized compounds in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on exciplex emission is demonstrated. The advanced co-deposition technique with the tuned OLED architecture was applied and resulted in improved OLED parameters.

sources.title: Treat-through OLED Displays: Dosimetry and performance of OLED AVATAR screens for Megavoltage Radiotherapy
sources.abstract: The AVATAR system utilizes a radiolucent video display to help relax and immobilize pediatric patients during radiotherapy. This study investigates the use of OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) displays, which offer superior image quality and faster alignment compared to traditional projector-based systems, albeit with slightly increased thickness. The dose perturbations caused by these screens were assessed to evaluate their suitability for radiotherapy. A 20 cm OLED screen was positioned in the patient's line of sight, between the patient's head and the radiation source. The screen comprises a 0.25 mm thick flexible OLED panel and a custom carbon fiber backing (0.3 to 0.6 mm thick), with most electronic components relocated via ribbon cable. 6 MV portal images were captured with and without the screen to create transmission maps. Additionally, parallel plate ion chamber measurements were taken at the surface and at depth in a solid water phantom. The OLED's radiation tolerance was tested with a 100 Gy dose delivery and 12 months of use in an active radiotherapy linac vault. The portal image transmission maps indicated an average attenuation difference of 0.3\% (SD = 0.37 \%) between measurements with and without the AVATAR screen, with a maximum point attenuation of 3\%. Ion chamber measurements revealed a 0.31\% decrease in dose at 2 cm depth and a 7.04 \% increase at the surface under an anterior-posterior beam. For a VMAT arc, the dose difference was 0.04 \% at 2 cm depth and 0.1\% at the phantom surface. The minimal dose deviations indicate that these screens are suitable for megavoltage arc therapy without significantly affecting the target dose. While surface dose is slightly increased for static anterior beams, it remains low. For lower photon energies or particle beams, larger perturbations may occur, necessitating further measurements or beam entry avoidance.

sources.title: Vacuum Thermal Evaporation for OLEDs: Fundamentals, Optimization, and Implications for Perovskite LEDs
sources.abstract: Abstract Organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) are central to high‐end displays and solid‐state lighting due to their small thickness and high flexibility, wide color gamut, and low power consumption. While solution processing offers simplicity and cost advantages for polymer‐based OLEDs, vacuum thermal evaporation (VTE) remains the dominant method for the commercial production of high‐performance small‐molecule OLEDs, owing to its precise control over film thickness, material purity, and multilayer integration. However, to meet the demands of display applications for higher performance, lower cost and more diverse forms (such as flexibility and high resolution), it is crucial to continuously optimize the VTE process. Meanwhile, although solution processing remains the predominant approach for perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs), recent exploratory efforts have investigated VTE as an alternative route, thereby opening opportunities to transfer process insights from OLEDs to PeLEDs. This review aims to systematically summarize the application foundation and optimization strategies of VTE technology in OLEDs, and to explore how these mature practices can inform the process development and device design of vacuum‐evaporated PeLEDs.

findings.claim: OLED degradation (burn-in/image sticking) remains an acknowledged reliability issue across several application areas (VR microdisplays, automotive, inkjet-printed panels), and compensation algorithms are described as only partly effective.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Three abstracts from different contexts point to the same problem. The VR simulation (src_50f14aa505) uses a stretched-exponential model and surrogate image content, so it is simulation-based, with no hardware validation stated in the abstract. The IJP OLED paper (src_f11da0f8c8) says de-burn-in 'cannot be completely improved' because of lifetime variation, and its fix is a per-panel manufacturing step that adds process complexity. The automotive paper (src_125ddf53dd) lists lifetime and burn-in as known challenges. All three are conference papers and are not full peer-reviewed studies.

findings.claim: The VR burn-in result depends on assumed image content and head-motion data, so the stated 4x slower time to visual failure is an assumption-dependent simulation result rather than a measured lifetime.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The abstract reports a 'conservative assumption' and surrogate content for 'productivity and gaming mode'. It says nothing about validation on physical devices or about content outside those two modes. Generalising to real use is a gap.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Given a conservative assumption for image content and head motion, the time for visual failure due to burn-in artifacts is 4 times slower than a case with stationary image content.

findings.claim: Physical efficiency and stability limits persist at high brightness: bimolecular annihilation (TTA/TPA) causes efficiency roll-off, heat and chemical damage, and blue emitter stability is still named as an open research priority.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: A thesis (src_8078af2390) and a review (src_4dd4177962) both frame roll-off and stability as persistent. The thesis says mitigation requires a 'constant balance' with manufacturing complexity. Neither abstract quantifies how far the problem is from being solved commercially.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Future research should focus particularly on improving the stability of blue emitters and developing more precise kinetic models to ensure the reliability of mass-produced devices.

findings.claim: Large-area OLED manufacturing is cost- and complexity-constrained. Vacuum thermal evaporation dominates for high-performance small-molecule OLEDs, and inkjet printing, the proposed scalable route, is still described as a research-stage candidate with unresolved issues.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The inkjet review (src_1ae66a9e98) says conventional evaporation makes uniform large-area fabrication costly and complex. The VTE review (src_b9cbb54562) says VTE remains dominant for commercial high-performance OLEDs. The IJP image-sticking paper (src_f11da0f8c8) shows that printed OLEDs still face lifetime-variation problems. The abstracts do not give yield or cost data, so the timing is a judgement. Evidence rests on reviews and one conference abstract.

findings.claim: Competing display technologies are presented as potential displacers in demanding segments. LCDs with full-array local dimming are cost-competitive in automotive, and micro-LED and electrically pumped QD are said to have potential to outperform both.
findings.label: unverified_claim
findings.rationale: This is one invited conference abstract, and 'potential' is not demonstrated performance. The horizon is a loose reading. Its OLED advantages (response time at low temperature, black level) are stated alongside high-luminance and temperature sensitivity.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Latest automotive demonstrators show the potential of micro-LEDs and electrically pumped Quantum Dots (QD) displays. Both have the potential to outperform LCDs and OLEDs.

findings.claim: Automotive use faces specific constraints: high luminance and temperature sensitivity reduce OLED lifetime, and LCDs benefit from a large supply chain and competitive cost.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Single abstract, no quantitative data given. Only 'some premium OEMs' are said to ship OLED cars, which suggests narrow adoption, though the abstract does not measure share.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Well‐known challenges of OLEDs deal with high luminance and temperature sensitivity, which can result in reduced lifetime (LT) incl. Burn‐In.

findings.claim: Electrically pumped organic lasing has been shown only through an indirect OLED-pumped structure, because direct charge injection into organic gain media causes intolerable losses. This limits readiness for any laser-based OLED-adjacent application.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The Nature abstract describes a first demonstration with a threshold and a beam. It says direct injection is 'very challenging' because of low current density and absorption from charges and triplets. The abstract gives no data on lifetime, power or efficiency, so commercial readiness is a gap. The relevance to display investment is indirect.

findings.claim: Some of the OLED-related work retrieved is niche, early-stage or narrow in scope, giving little evidence of broad commercial robustness.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The radiotherapy display study (src_dc5ddf0cb0) is an arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed, and tests one screen type, though it reports a 100 Gy tolerance test and 12 months of use. The fluorene study (src_c6711d3ba9) demonstrates exciplex OLEDs with 'improved parameters' without stating figures, so the size of the gain is unknown. Neither addresses mass-market durability.

hype_flags: 'Exponential upsurge' in OLED demand tied to IoT (src_1ae66a9e98): the abstract gives no data behind the phrase.
Inkjet printing as 'pre-eminent candidate' for scalable OLED manufacturing (src_1ae66a9e98): the abstract is promotional, and the companion IJP paper still reports image-sticking problems.
'Improved OLED parameters' for fluorene derivatives (src_c6711d3ba9): no figures are given in the abstract.

Micro-LED and electrically pumped QD 'potential to outperform' OLED (src_125ddf53dd): potential rather than demonstrated, and a similar caution applies to claims about hyperphosphorescent OLEDs solving stability.

finding.claim: S1 overstates progress. The abstract says deep-blue PHOLEDs are 'achieving lifetimes approaching those of their green analogs'. That is not the same as having 'improved substantially' or being adoption-ready. The same abstract says 100% internal efficiency PHOLEDs have still not met the stability standards needed for adoption. S1 also comes from a single perspective article, which is not independent evidence or a quantified benchmark. Its 'verified_fact' label hides the tension with S2 and with the thesis on blue emitter stability, which still lists it as a research priority.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstract has no lifetime numbers, metrics or conditions (LT50, luminance, colour coordinates). 'Approaching' is a qualitative claim by the authors. S1 and S2 should be read together: S1 is a hopeful trend and S2 is the unresolved status. The thesis src_8078af2390 independently names blue emitter stability as a future research priority.

finding.claim: S3 is vague and its framing is weak. The abstract only says the authors 'address some persistent problems commonly found in the literature' on measuring quantum efficiency and operational lifetime. It does not say these measurements are unreliable overall. It also does not say how this affects the lifetime claims in S1. If lifetime measurement is inconsistent, that is a direct caveat on S1's comparison with green lifetimes, and the findings do not link the two.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: This is an interpretation. The abstract flags measurement problems but gives no detail. Even so, S1's headline lifetime comparison is exposed to the measurement-quality caveat that S3 notes separately. Both findings use the same source.

finding.claim: S9, S10 and S13 are simulation, psychophysical or lab-testbed results that are presented as 'verified_fact' with little caveat. S9's 31% power saving is a reported figure from a perceptual study and is combined with prior luminance dimming. 'No statistical loss' is relative to a perceptual loss budget and the participant pool. S10 is a model-development preprint. All three are single, non-peer-reviewed arXiv preprints, so readiness is not shown.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: All three are arXiv preprints with abstract-only access. S9's 31% needs to be read as 'combined with prior work on luminance dimming', not as a stand-alone gain. S10 has no stated accuracy figure and no real-hardware validation. S13 tests one specific metalens design, so it does not generalise to all metalenses.

finding.claim: S7 and S6 rest on one-sentence trade-press blurbs with no data. 'Breakthrough' and 'enable a wider range of applications' are promotional statements, not verified results. S6 has the same problem: 'polaritons solve this issue' is an unquantified assertion, and the paper has 0 citations. Labelling these 'verified_fact' is not justified, because only the existence of the claim is verified.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstracts give no metrics, test conditions or evidence. They cannot support any substantive finding about the technologies. S7 in particular says almost nothing about what the 'MAX' solution is.

The findings ignore the competitive and reliability caveats found elsewhere. In automotive, LCDs have 'a large supply chain', and micro-LED and QD displays are said to have potential to outperform OLEDs. Burn-in and temperature-related lifetime limits also remain.

finding.claim: S14 claims 'little cross-citation evident' between two tracks, but the evidence has only titles and abstracts and no citation data. Cross-citation cannot be inferred from them. The split also reflects the sampling by search queries. The findings do not test the claim, so it is an artefact rather than a property of the literature. Some sources in the sample bridge the tracks, for example the burn-in and VR lifetime simulation and the stability-focused hyperphosphorescent work.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: No reference lists were available, so the cross-citation claim cannot be assessed. The VR burn-in simulation (src_50f14aa505) links device degradation with system and content effects, which weakens the 'largely separate' framing.

finding.claim: S15 draws a conclusion about 'mature, low-cost, commodity use' of OLED modules from four hobbyist or educational embedded-systems papers, and this does not show anything about the OLED technology. These papers mention an OLED only as a component, and several are low-impact preprints with no citations. They are not evidence about OLED maturity or the research frontier. They probably entered the sample because of keyword matching and should be excluded as noise, not interpreted as a trend.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstracts name OLED displays as one component of each system and make no claims about their maturity, cost or commodity status. The only cost-related statement is the muon detector's under $100 total component cost, which is for the whole device.
finding.supporting_excerpt: An OLED display shows the status of parking slots in real-time.

finding.claim: The Science findings omit reliability and manufacturing risks that appear in the retrieved evidence. These include burn-in and image sticking, which compensation algorithms only partly resolve, efficiency roll-off from bimolecular annihilation at high brightness, and the cost and complexity of large-area manufacturing (evaporation is dominant while inkjet printing remains an unfinished candidate). Several Science findings (S4, S5, S8, S11) are descriptive or optimistic and carry none of these risks.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The excerpt shows that image sticking compensation is incomplete. The thesis and the inkjet review add that roll-off and large-area manufacturing remain limits.
finding.supporting_excerpt: One solution to IS is De‐burn‐in technology (DBI), but it cannot be completely improved due to deviation in OLED life characteristics.

limitations: Only titles and abstracts were reviewed. Several abstracts are truncated and quantitative detail is missing.
Only 12 papers were provided, several off-topic or tangential to display investment (organic laser, radiotherapy, fluorene chemistry).
Coverage lacks market, cost, yield, supply-chain and company-specific evidence, so risks such as supplier concentration cannot be assessed.
Some evidence is conference abstracts, a thesis or an arXiv preprint (src_dc5ddf0cb0), which are not fully peer reviewed.
Absence of data on blue-emitter lifetime, large-area yield or power consumption in these abstracts is a gap, not evidence of failure.
Only titles, metadata and abstracts were available. Claims may be better supported in the full papers.
Several sources are trade-magazine blurbs with one or two sentences, so I could not judge their substance.
Many cited works are arXiv preprints and are not peer reviewed. I did not check for later published versions.
The evidence set is small (27 papers) and reflects search queries, so absence of contradicting evidence is weak evidence.
I did not challenge S2, S4, S5, S8 or S12 because the abstracts support them closely.

market.coverage_note: Company evidence is limited to short verbatim passages from the latest SEC annual/quarterly reports of the companies in config/companies.yaml that mention the keywords. 8-K press releases (exhibit files) are not read, and companies that do not file with the SEC (e.g. SK hynix, Samsung) are not covered. Company size and trend figures (revenue, growth, R&D, net income) come from the SEC's XBRL company-facts data as reported by each company; the size class is by revenue, not market value. Companies marked 'discovered' were found by a full-text search of all SEC filings for the topic phrase; they are not on the configured list, are often small, and a mention in a filing says nothing about their size, role or prospects.

findings.rationale: Two separate posts report Apple's OLED transition timing and pricing; both are second-hand reports/leaks with stated 2027 timing, so horizon is medium-term. Numbers come only from the posts.

findings.claim: Tandem OLED is appearing as a marketing differentiator across multiple consumer devices this week: Motorola's Signature 27 launched globally with a 6.8-inch Tandem OLED display at $1,599+, and Apple's MacBook Pro OLED is described as tandem ('PROLED XDR').
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Independent accounts (Techmeme citing 9to5Google, PaidFreeDroid, and the Apple-leaker account) all emphasise tandem OLED in flagship devices within the same week, suggesting the technology is a current premium-panel trend.

findings.rationale: Vendor self-promotion (ShapesXR promoting its own integration); the micro-OLED specification is the partner's claim, repeated across four near-identical posts.

findings.claim: OLED is spreading across mainstream laptop line-ups: HP launched OmniBook 5 14 and ProBook 4 G2iS 14 in India with OLED displays, and Google 'Googlebook OS' devices are leaked with up to 13-inch OLED displays.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Two independent sources in the same week point to OLED moving into mid-range laptops and a new device category; both are press/leak posts, not verified specs.

findings.claim: OLED monitors are becoming affordable: Tom's Hardware highlighted a 27-inch 240Hz Acer Nitro OLED gaming monitor at $269, and Asus's ProArt PA329CDV offers a 32-inch 4K 120Hz professional OLED at $899.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Two independent press accounts within days report aggressively priced OLED monitors, a consistent signal of OLED monitor price erosion at both gaming and professional tiers.

findings.claim: Gaming-tournament use still favours LCD monitors, but Engadget argues regular gamers should embrace OLED displays — indicating OLED vs LCD debate persists in the gaming-monitor segment.
findings.label: unverified_claim
findings.rationale: Editorial opinion from Engadget; the linked article was not read, so only the headline claim is available.

limitations: 7-day window only; this captures a news spike (largely Apple MacBook Pro OLED coverage) and not long-term trends.
Fixed account list skewed toward semiconductors/AI; few dedicated display-industry accounts (no Samsung Display, LG Display, BOE, UDC etc.), so panel-maker statements are absent.
Much content is from leaker/enthusiast accounts (@craigapplecom, @TechieUltimatum) and promotional vendor posts (ShapesXR, BLU Products); claims are marketing or rumour, not verified.
Linked articles (TrendForce, Macworld, The Verge, 9to5Google) were not read; only post text was analysed.
No posts from core semiconductor/standards accounts in the list mention OLED this week, so supply-chain and equipment signals are missing.
Posting volume is low-to-moderate; quiet accounts are not evidence of inactivity.

draft.summary: OLED displays are a technology already in volume use. Company filings describe a multi-layer supply chain (materials licensing, equipment, glass, drivers, panels) and say OLED is gaining share in phones, TVs, monitors, laptops, AR/VR and automotive [M1, M2, M10]. Research output is rising (394 to 467 works, +18.5% in 2025, and 600 vs 358 year to date in 2026), but the count is not normalised for overall publishing growth, and patent filings are flat at roughly 220 a year [P1-P4]. Open technical and commercial issues remain: blue-emitter stability, burn-in, efficiency roll-off, the cost of large-area manufacturing, and competition from LCD and, reportedly, micro-LED [S2, R1, R3, R4, R5]. Several Science findings were challenged as overstated or based on weak sources [C1, C4, C5, C7]. Social-media signals about Apple and tandem OLED are unverified. The main uncertainty is whether OLED keeps widening into IT, automotive and AR/VR against cheaper or newer rivals. This is a research assessment, not investment advice.
draft.plain_summary: OLED screens are the kind of display now common in premium phones and increasingly in laptops, monitors and cars. The evidence says they are already widely made and sold, and research on them keeps growing. The main thing that could slow them down is that the blue light-emitting material still wears out faster than the others, and big screens remain expensive to make compared with older LCD screens.

themes.name: OLED spreading from phones into laptops, monitors and cars

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Filings say OLED is gaining share across phones, TVs, monitors, laptops and automotive, and Samsung Display is working with Dolby on automotive OLED [M2, M9]. Social posts point to tandem OLED launches, cheaper OLED monitors and broader laptop use [X4, X6, X7]. These posts are signals, not verified facts. Burn-in and automotive temperature limits are open reliability issues [R1, R6].

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Reported Apple plans (up to 1.5 million OLED MacBook Pro units in 2027, with possible removal of mini-LED models) would be a major demand signal if true. They come from supply-chain reports relayed on social media and are unverified [X2, X3]. LCD with local dimming is cost-competitive in automotive, and the claim that micro-LED or QD could displace OLED is unverified [R5, R6].

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: The evidence says little directly about 3-5 years. Whether OLED holds share depends on cost reduction, lifetime and competing technologies, none of which the findings resolve. Flexible OLED is described as dominant in premium smartphones, but the support is a trade-magazine abstract without market data [S11, C5].

bull.label: forecast
bull.narrative: Tandem OLED and falling panel prices carry OLED into mainstream laptops, monitors and cars. Panel makers and the suppliers around them see steady volume growth [M2, M9, X4, X7].

base.label: forecast
base.narrative: OLED keeps gaining share in premium and mid-range devices. LCD stays competitive on cost in segments such as automotive and tournament gaming, and reliability and cost remain moderating factors [R6, X8, M2].

bear.label: forecast
bear.narrative: Burn-in, high-temperature lifetime limits and cost keep OLED out of demanding segments. Cost-competitive LCD, or newer micro-LED, takes the share that was expected to go to OLED [R1, R5, R6].

themes.name: Blue-emitter lifetime and low-cost manufacturing for OLED

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Blue pixels use roughly half the front-plane energy, and stable 100%-efficiency blue PHOLEDs have not met adoption standards [S2]. The claim that deep-blue lifetimes are approaching green rests on one perspective article and was challenged [S1, C1]. Evaporation dominates large-area production, and inkjet printing is still research-stage [R4]. Equipment suppliers sell into LCD and OLED production [M7].

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Patent filings on inspection, defect detection and polyimide or coating materials show continued industrial effort [P2, P3]. Whether blue stability or inkjet printing reaches production in this window is not shown by the evidence. Lifetime measurement problems weaken any cross-lab comparison [S3, C2].

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: No finding gives a timeline for solving blue stability or scaling printed OLED. A breakthrough is possible but unsupported, and the cost-of-ownership benefit is not quantified [S2, R4].

bull.label: forecast
bull.narrative: Blue PHOLED or MR-TADF emitters reach production lifetimes and inkjet printing matures. Panel efficiency rises and large-area cost falls, benefiting materials and equipment suppliers [S1, R3, R4].

base.label: forecast
base.narrative: Incremental improvements continue, but blue stability stays a named research priority and evaporation remains the main production method [S2, R3, R4].

bear.label: forecast

risks.label: ai_interpretation

risks.label: ai_interpretation

companies.label: ai_interpretation

companies.relevance: Its Display segment sells manufacturing equipment for LCD and OLED displays. OLED is one part of a larger business.

companies.relevance: Has begun producing OLED displays and makes protective films for OLED panels. It is micro by revenue (about 0.04B USD, +22.2%), so it carries higher risk and less disclosure. It is not a recommendation.

themes.name: Micro-OLED for AR/VR and smart glasses

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Micro-OLED is being positioned in AR glasses (XREAL AURA, unverified social post) [X5]. Vuzix ships an OLED product (M400) but its newer glasses use microLED [M5]. Patent filings target Micro-OLED light extraction and silicon anodes [P1]. VR burn-in remains a reliability issue [R1, R2].

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Filings show Kopin investing R&D in OLED microdisplays alongside MicroLED and defense products [M4]. Customer adoption is not evidenced in the findings. Polariton and metalens optics are early, and the metalens work reports ghosting under realistic OLED illumination [S6, S13, C4].

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: The evidence gives no basis for sizing the AR/VR OLED market. Competition from microLED is visible in Vuzix's newer products [M5], and micro-LED potential is a claim from a single source [R5].

bull.label: forecast
bull.narrative: Micro-OLED becomes the standard microdisplay for AR/VR and smart glasses as light extraction improves and consumer devices ship in volume [P1, X5, S11].

base.label: forecast
base.narrative: Micro-OLED coexists with microLED in niche, high-end and defense products, with burn-in and optics still being worked on [M4, M5, R1].

bear.label: forecast
bear.narrative: MicroLED displaces OLED microdisplays in smart glasses and burn-in limits VR adoption. Small microdisplay companies struggle financially [M5, R1, R5, T1].

catalysts.label: unverified_claim
catalysts.text: Volume consumer smart-glasses products using micro-OLED, beyond the announced XREAL product.

catalysts.label: forecast

dimension_ratings.rationale: RISK SCALE level 2 (moderate): OLED is shipping in volume with real customers and several suppliers [M1, M2, M6, M9, M10], but has clear open issues: blue emitter stability, burn-in, high-brightness roll-off, large-area cost and competition from LCD and possibly micro-LED [S2, R1, R3, R4, R5]. Risk challenges were medium severity [C1, C5, C8]. Kopin's price pullback and very high volatility add timing and small-company risk for microdisplay exposure [T1, T2], but do not raise the technology-level rating.

Independent, standardised blue-emitter lifetime benchmarks and measured burn-in data.
Cost comparisons of OLED against LCD, micro-LED and QD displays.
Verification of the Apple OLED MacBook Pro volumes and pricing, and of the XREAL and Motorola specifications (social-media reports only).
Citation and peer-review information for the research findings (abstract-level only; some are preprints).

Financial evidence for several small companies flagged by the scout (e.g., Fabric.AI, Photronics, PPG) and for non-SEC-listed patent assignees; their connection to OLED displays is not substantiated by cited findings.
limitations: Science findings are based on titles and abstracts of a sample of papers, several of them single perspective articles, trade abstracts or preprints, and some were successfully challenged by the Risk agent [C1-C7].
Research counts are not normalised for overall growth in publishing and include papers that use OLED only as a component [S15, C7].
Patent counts for recent years are undercounted because of publication delay, and applications are claims, not proof of commercial use.
X posts are social signals and rumours, not facts. Company filing excerpts show what companies say, not independently verified results.
Price and timing data (Kopin only, about 100 trading days) is risk context, not a signal or a view on future prices.
This is a cautious research assessment, not a recommendation, price target or forecast of returns.
